intents.text: Add starlette/middleware/body_limit.py with a pure ASGI RequestBodyLimitMiddleware(app, max_body_size: int) that wraps receive, counts the body bytes actually received (including multipart data and encoding overhead), and answers with a plain-text 413 Content Too Large when the total exceeds max_body_size.

Use Content-Length only as a fail-fast check (declared length over the limit is rejected before the body is read), while absent or understated headers never bypass the received-byte count, and a body exactly at the limit is allowed.
If the app has already started a response when the limit is crossed, the middleware sends no second response but the limit still stops the receive stream (raises/terminates).
Add a max_body_size: int | None = None keyword to Starlette, Router, Mount and Route, where None keeps today's unlimited behaviour.

Apply the Starlette-level limit through the middleware stack before routing (so application middleware reading the body is limited), and let an inner Route/Mount/Router limit override the outer one after routing, both raising and lowering it.
In starlette/formparsers.py, close any temporary files the multipart parser created whenever parsing is interrupted for any reason, including a body-limit error raised mid-stream.

Add tests covering the middleware (with/without Content-Length, understated Content-Length, exactly-at-limit, multipart, streaming bodies, no double response), max_body_size on Starlette/Router/Mount/Route including inner raising and lowering the outer limit, and multipart temp-file cleanup.

constraints: Export nothing new at the package root; import the middleware from starlette.middleware.body_limit
Existing test suite must stay green
Default max_body_size=None must preserve current unlimited behaviour
